intent_en: To illustrate why lawmakers target capital gains tax reform by demonstrating that the majority of long-term capital gains are concentrated among the top 1% of earners.
previous_intent: To illustrate the heavy concentration of long-term capital gains among the highest income earners in 2018, thereby explaining why lawmakers consider capital gains tax reform an easy way to tax the wealthy.
narration_support: most taxable capital gains are going to the top 1%
chart_support: Donut chart showing long-term capital gains distribution by income group in 2018, where the top 1% segment represents the majority share compared to everyone else.
evidence_note: The narration explicitly links the concentration of gains in the top 1% to lawmakers' motivation to tax the rich. The chart visualizes this with the top 1% (orange) taking up the larger portion of the donut chart (labeled 69%) compared to everyone else.
